sentences.text:
This writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs:
"(i) For issuance of direction upon the Respondents particularly Respondent no. 4 to 6 to immediately and forthwith send to this Hon'ble Court all records appertaining to the acquisition of land relating to Mouza-Brindabanpur, Mouza No.- 64, Khata No.
29, Plot No. 236/441, Area-7 Decimal at P.S. Nirsha, District-Dhanbad.
AND (II) For issuance of writ in the nature of mandamus commanding upon the Respondents to pay compensation for demolishing the house of the petitioner without acquisition of land under the National Highways Act, 1956;
AND (iii) For issuance of direction in the nature of mandamus commanding upon the Respondents to pay damages for demolishing the house of the petitioner and causing damages to other structure situated over the land despite the fact that the land of the petitioner was never notified under 3 (D) Notification."
4. From perusal of para 12 of the writ records it appears that vide memo No. 1473 dated 09.12.2021 issued by the District Land Acquisition Dhanbad to the Project Director, National Highway Authority of India, Durgapur , a direction was given to get the land of the petitioner demarcated which was scheduled on 21.12.2021 so that his grievance may be redressed, but the Project Director,
NHAI, Durgapur, never acted upon the same.
5.

The counsel for the petitioner has submitted that had the demarcation been done, it could have revealed as to whether the property which is being claimed by the petitioner has been acquired or not and as to whether the property which has been demolished was within the acquired portion of the land or not.

6. Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No. 2 to 4 has submitted that in case the demarcation has not been done as stated by the petitioner in paragraph 12 of the writ petition, then there is no impediment in demarcating the acquired area.

7. She submits that no counter affidavit has been filed in the present case and if the demarcation has already been done pursuant to the letter dated 09.12.2021, then there may not be any occasion for fresh demarcation and the document regarding demarcation can be handed over to the petitioner for needful.
She has also submitted that for the demarcation of land, the assistance of the respondent No. 5,6 and 7 will also be required.

8. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this court is of the considered view that the petitioner had made a request for demarcation of the land and consequently a letter dated 09.12.2021 was also issued for the purposes of demarcation, but as per the writ petition, the required demarcation was not done.

10. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of enabling the petitioner to approach the respondent No. 6 along with this order and a copy of the writ records and a detailed representation with all supporting documents.
Upon his filing of representation, the respondent No. 6 shall do the needful so that demarcation is done in terms of the letter dated 09.12.2021 (Annexure-7) in presence of the petitioner.
The other respondent authorities i.e Respondent No. 5,6 and 7 are also directed to co-operate in the matter of demarcation of land.
The needful be done within a period of one month from the date of receipt of the representation.
Upon demarcation, if the petitioner has any surviving grievance, it shall be open to the petitioner to take steps in accordance with law.

11. It is however observed that if the demarcation has already been done pursuant to the letter dated 09.12.2021, no fresh demarcation is required to be done and the document showing the demarcation of land be handed over to the petitioner.
12.
This writ petition is accordingly disposed of.
13. Pending I.A., if any, is closed.
